questions.subject: Science
questions.stem: A Class 9 student is tracing where the word ‘cell’ first entered biology, and finds that the name was given in 1665 to structures seen in a thin slice of cork. Consider the following statements. 1. Robert Hooke was the first person to observe a cell, in 1665, and he did so using a self-designed microscope. 2. He was able to do this because that self-designed microscope was capable of about 200–300X magnification, which allowed him to make out the small box-like compartments in the cork slice. Choose the correct option. (A) Both the assertion and the reason are true and the reason is a correct explanation of the assertion. (B) Both the assertion and the reason are true but the reason is not a correct explanation of the assertion. (C) The assertion is true but the reason is false. (D) Both the assertion and the reason are false.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: Both the assertion and the reason are true and the reason is a correct explanation of the assertion.

questions.subject: Science
questions.stem: A Class 9 student wants the real size of the cells in an onion peel. The student places a transparent ruler with millimetre (mm) markings on the stage of the microscope, focuses on it with the adjustment knob, and measures the diameter of the circular field of view through the eyepiece. Consider the following statements. 1. The diameter measured in mm must then be converted into micrometre (µm); a visible field of 5 mm is written as 5 × 1000 = 5000 µm. 2. No such conversion is needed, because a transparent ruler with millimetre (mm) markings can be read straight off as a measurement in micrometre (µm). Choose the correct option. (A) Both the assertion and the reason are true and the reason is a correct explanation of the assertion. (B) Both the assertion and the reason are true but the reason is not a correct explanation of the assertion. (C) The assertion is true but the reason is false. (D) Both the assertion and the reason are false.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: The assertion is true but the reason is false.

questions.subject: Science
questions.stem: A Class 9 student must produce an image showing the fine details of a cell structure and can choose between the school light microscope, which uses 10X and 40X objective lenses under visible light, and an electron microscope. Consider the following statements. 1. The school light microscope alone is enough to reveal the fine details of a cell structure. 2. The reason is that an electron microscope forms its image from a beam of light rather than a beam of electrons, so it can show what the light microscope cannot. Choose the correct option. (A) Both the assertion and the reason are true and the reason is a correct explanation of the assertion. (B) Both the assertion and the reason are true but the reason is not a correct explanation of the assertion. (C) The assertion is true but the reason is false. (D) Both the assertion and the reason are false.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: Both the assertion and the reason are false.
